Śibi
------------------------------------------
Śibi—also known as Vṛṣādarbhi—was a king of काशी. He had taken a vow that he would protect anyone who took refuge in him. Once इन्द्र and अग्नि decided to subject him to a severe test. इन्द्र took the form of a hawk and अग्नि, that of a pigeon. The hawk started pursuing the pigeon to kill it and eat it. The pigeon managed to approach the king शिबि and sought his protection which he instantly promised. When the hawk too approached him to give the pigeon which was its rightful ड़ोओद्, शिबि struck a compromise saying that he would give as much flesh as the pigeon weighed, from his own body. When he started cutting his own body, the two gods revealed themselves in their true form, appreciated his sacrifice and gave him several boons including making his body whole as it was earlier, (vide Mahābhārata, Vanaparva, 197).
